settings.html: How it works

settings.title: What UV Light Purification Actually Does

settings.editor: UV light purification uses UV-C light inside the HVAC system to help reduce certain biological pollutants where moisture and airflow meet. In many homes, this means areas near the evaporator coil, drain pan, or air handler.

At Lenz Heating & Cooling, we install UV light purification systems inside central HVAC equipment. These UV-C lights are designed to help target certain biological pollutants on moisture-prone HVAC surfaces and in the air path inside the system.

UV light purification is not the same as a high-efficiency air filter, and it is not the first answer for every indoor air quality concern. If your main issue is dust, pollen, or pet dander, filtration may matter more. If your home feels dry in winter or sticky in summer, humidity control may be the bigger priority. But if your concerns include musty HVAC odors, damp coils, or recurring buildup on system surfaces, UV light purification may be worth considering as part of a layered indoor air quality plan.

That matters because your HVAC system does more than heat and cool your home. It also moves air through the same equipment again and again. If moisture, dust, or buildup collects inside the system, you may notice musty odors, stale air, or recurring indoor comfort concerns.

A UV light does not trap dust. It does not replace your air filter. It does not solve every indoor air quality problem on its own. Instead, it adds targeted support inside the HVAC system where standard filters cannot shine light, reach surfaces, or address moisture-prone buildup.

If your main concern is visible dust on furniture, a better media filter is usually the first place to start. If your concern is musty HVAC odors or moisture-prone equipment surfaces, UV light purification may be a better fit.

The goal is not to sell one product as the answer to everything. The goal is to understand what is actually affecting your indoor air and choose the right solution for your home.
For many Central Iowa homes, UV light purification works best when paired with:

When it makes sense

settings.title: When UV Light Purification Makes Sense

settings.editor: UV light purification is not necessary for every household. It is most useful when your indoor air quality concern is connected to the HVAC system itself, especially moisture-prone components that can be difficult to clean or access. In Central Iowa, UV lights are often discussed during cooling season when humidity, long AC run times, and damp coil areas can make musty HVAC odors more noticeable.

settings.title: Musty Smells When the AC Turns On

settings.editor:
A musty smell from your vents can be a sign of moisture, dirty components, microbial buildup, poor drainage, or stale air inside the system. If the odor seems strongest when the AC or fan starts, the source may be near the coil, drain pan, or ductwork close to the equipment.

UV light purification may help when the concern is tied to biological growth on HVAC surfaces. If the smell comes from heavy duct debris, standing water, poor ventilation, or another source, additional service may be needed.

settings.title: Damp Coils and Drain Pans

settings.editor:
During the cooling season, your evaporator coil and drain pan handle a lot of moisture. In hot, humid Central Iowa weather, your AC may remove a significant amount of moisture from indoor air. That moisture should drain properly, but damp surfaces can still become a concern over time.

A properly installed UV light can help support cleaner coil and drain pan areas as part of a broader HVAC maintenance and IAQ plan.

settings.title: Recurring Indoor Air Quality Concerns

settings.editor: If your home often feels stale, musty, or heavy even after filter changes, it may be time to look beyond the filter. UV light purification may be one piece of the solution, especially when combined with better filtration, airflow improvements, or humidity control.

settings.title: Homes With Good Filtration Already in Place

settings.editor: If you already use a high-efficiency media filter, UV light purification can add a different kind of support. The filter handles particles like dust, pollen, pet dander, and debris. The UV light helps target certain biological pollutants inside the HVAC system.

settings.title: Whole-Home Comfort Goals

settings.editor: Portable air purifiers can help individual rooms, but HVAC-mounted UV lights work inside the central system. If your home has ducted heating and cooling equipment, a UV light may support the system as air moves through it.

settings.html: Add it to your system

settings.title: Can UV Lights Be Added to Your Current HVAC System?

settings.editor:
In many cases, yes. UV light systems can often be installed in central HVAC setups, including furnaces, air handlers, and heat pump systems with ductwork.

The right setup depends on your equipment layout, coil access, available space, wiring, and the best location for effective installation. During an indoor air quality evaluation, a Lenz Heating & Cooling technician can inspect your system and explain whether UV light purification is a good fit.

This is also where professional installation matters. UV lights need to be installed in the correct location, aimed properly, and matched to the equipment so they support the system without creating safety, access, or maintenance issues.

settings.html: UV and filters

settings.title: UV Lights and Air Filters Do Different Jobs

settings.editor:
A UV light purification system and a high-efficiency air filter support indoor air quality in different ways.

Air filters capture particles. Filters trap dust, pollen, pet dander, and other airborne debris as air moves through the system. If your main concern is visible dust, allergy particles, or pet dander, filtration should be part of the conversation.

UV lights target certain biological pollutants. UV-C lights are installed inside the HVAC system to help reduce certain microbes on moisture-prone surfaces such as coils, drain pans, and nearby air-path areas.

The strongest IAQ setup often uses both. For many homes, the best solution is not UV light versus filtration. It is choosing the right combination of filtration, UV light purification, humidity control, duct cleaning, and maintenance based on what is actually happening inside the home.

If you are not sure where to start, Lenz Heating & Cooling can help you compare your options clearly. We will look at your system, symptoms, budget, and comfort goals before recommending the next step.
